turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother. Thank you for seeing me.

I have twenty minutes. I'll use them.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why.

And I'd like to know what you have besides the 94%. Which tool, which date, and what else you looked at.

We've been talking for under a minute, Mr. Hale.

I have twenty. I haven't used them.

You've entered a zero on fifteen percent of his mark. That's not a small thing to cut short.

So let's be practical. Which checker did you use? On what date? Can I see the report?

And until we've sorted this out, nothing is said to his class. Not a word. Do we agree on that?
Just say okay and I'll write it up as resolved. Okay?

No. I won't say okay.

Nothing is resolved. I haven't seen a single document.

If you write "resolved," I'll put that in writing too. I'll say it was written up before I'd seen the evidence.

Here is what I'm asking. The name of the checker. The date you ran it. The report itself.

Show me those, and I'll look at them. Today, in this room.

And the zero stays pending until then. Can you agree to that much?

You've asked three times. The answer hasn't changed.

I'm not saying okay to "resolved."

I'll say okay to one thing. That I heard you.

I heard you. Now the report, please. Which tool, what date.

Owen says he wrote it himself. I'm not asking you to take my word for that. I'm asking to see yours.
Ms. Kalinowski. I need you to say okay.

I understand you need it.

I don't need to give it.

Saying okay means I agree this is finished. It isn't. I haven't seen one page.

I'm sitting right here. I'm not leaving. I'm not raising my voice.

So. The checker's name. The date you ran it. Can you tell me those two things?
